title: Causal Inference for All: Marginal Estimands for Outcomes Truncated by Death
summary: In longitudinal studies, outcomes of interest are often truncated by death, meaning that they are only observed or well-defined conditional on intercurrent events such as survival. Existing strategies face a trade-off: causally interpretable estimands, such as survivor average causal effects, target a latent subgroup, whereas while-alive and composite summaries apply to the full population but are difficult to interpret as causal effects on the non-mortality outcome. We address these challenges by introducing methodology for a new set of estimands that (i) concern the entire population, (ii)…
